Digital Duty of Care Bill 2026 (exposure draft)
snippet: exposure draft. Communications. This exposure draft would rewrite Part 2 of the Online Safety Act 2021 to impose a digital duty of care: anyone who provides or controls an online service would have to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, a safe online environment for people in Australia and for children in particular. Providers would have to manage design features such as recommender systems, endless feeds and engagement feedback, run written risk assessments at least once a year and act on them, with the eSafety Commissioner able to issue formal warnings and remedial directions and a civil penalty of up to 60,000 penalty units for a breach. It would also let the Commissioner order app stores and search engines to remove apps and links used to make fake nude material within 24 hours, open a data access scheme for approved researchers, and repeal the industry codes and standards of the online content scheme, with the duty of care commencing 12 months after assent.. Providers and controllers of online services used in Australia, including social media, messaging, search, app stores and generative AI services; children under 16 on social media; approved researchers; and the eSafety Commissioner.
